solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Getting on potty/loo tonight then?

indicators.note: potty means crazy, so the letters of the words that follow are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether an evening trip to the potty or loo means they are getting old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potty' looks like part of the bathroom picture, but it signals that LOO TONIGHT THEN is rearranged; the question mark admits the cheeky surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting on is an idiom for ageing, and the phrase originally judged a horse's age from its receding gums.

clue.text: Perhaps a "whole-fat pudding" is the precise legal definition

parts.note: the letter A is one example of a character of the alphabet, with perhaps marking the example

indicators.note: a pudding is a mixture stirred together, so the letters of whole-fat are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a rich dessert counts as a precise legal term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' says A is an instance of a LETTER; 'pudding' then mixes the eight letters of WHOLE-FAT into OF THE LAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping to the strict wording of a statute, rather than its spirit, is following its exact text.

clue.text: Finally open to offer: seed for Scandinavians

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of each of the three words open, to and offer

parts.note: seed is a synonym for semen

explanation.surface: An auction lot is finally open to bids, and the item for sale is seed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' applies to each of 'open', 'to' and 'offer' in turn, giving N, O and R.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vikings and other early peoples of Norway and its neighbours were called by this name.

clue.text: Bring on half of industry, then change sides

indicators.note: half of takes the first four of the eight letters of the word industry
the sides of a word are its first and last letters, here taken from change

explanation.surface: A factory owner brings in half the workforce and then switches allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change sides' reads as defecting, but 'sides' picks the first and last letters of 'change', C and E; 'then' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring on labour or sleep is to cause it artificially, as doctors do.

clue.text: See 1 across
See 15
Top of tatty, torn curtain becomes detached

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of the word tatty, since this is a down clue
torn suggests ripped apart, so the letters of curtain are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shabby curtain, ripped at the top, comes loose from its rail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torn' looks like a description of the curtain but rearranges its letters to ACITURN, after the T from 'Top of tatty'.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved, uncommunicative person seems aloof and emotionally distant.

clue.text: Riverside residents on the Thames estuary, rock stars originally

indicators.note: originally picks the opening letter of each of the six words before it

explanation.surface: Rock stars once lived in houses by the Thames estuary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock stars' seems to be the subject, but every word from 'on' to 'stars' just gives its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: These aquatic mammals make their dens, called holts, in river banks.

clue.text: What's up with the FT? Needs a revamp into a viable prominent position

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: eh is an informal way of asking what
taken as written

indicators.note: into means the jumbled letters are placed inside the next piece

parts.note: a viable plan is doable, able to be carried out

indicators.note: a revamp is a makeover, so the letters of the FT are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A reader asks what is wrong with the Financial Times, which needs a makeover to earn a leading place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns EH into HE; 'Needs a revamp' shuffles THEFT into FTHET, which 'into' places inside DOABLE after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The seat at the end of a dining board is traditionally the place of honour, kept for the host or chair.

clue.text: Abuse when Velia stops work

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so one piece is set inside the other

parts.note: a trade is a line of work
Velia is the setter, who refers to themselves as I

explanation.surface: The setter complains of being abused while taking a break from work.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter naming themselves means I, the first person; 'stops' puts it inside TRADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A long angry speech of denunciation is verbal abuse.

clue.text: Bacon sizzling here etc, cooked with thanks

parts.note: a frying pan is where food sizzles

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters have been doctored, so etc is rearranged

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: Bacon is frying in a pan along with other things, cooked with gratitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' looks like part of the kitchen scene but rearranges ETC into CET.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian cured pork belly is a kind of streaky bacon.

clue.text: Introduce Kathmandu's last shrine restoration

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word Kathmandu
a restoration rebuilds something, so the letters of shrine are rearranged

explanation.surface: Restoration of a temple in Nepal's capital is introduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restoration' sounds like building work but rearranges SHRINE into SHERIN, after the U ending Kathmandu.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring in or herald something new, like a season or era, is to introduce it.

clue.text: Work to banish the devil, as they say

indicators.note: as they say signals that the following is how the phrase is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: to drive out an evil spirit is to exorcise it

explanation.surface: A priest's job is to cast out demons, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: The two verbs sound nearly alike, differing only in one unstressed vowel.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical exertion to keep fit is a workout.

clue.text: Somewhat austere outfit for speaker?

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a plain suit is suitable for a person giving a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speaker' suggests a person addressing an audience, but it is a loudspeaker; the run sits inside 'austere outfit'.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-channel sound system is used with loudspeakers, and the word is often short for such a system.

clue.text: Rebel questionably dropped Latin from eulogy

indicators.note: to rebel is to rise up against order, so the remaining letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written as the larger pool of letters
taken as written, these letters are removed from the pool

explanation.surface: A rebellious speaker dubiously cut the Latin from a funeral address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' says the letters of LATIN come out of QUESTIONABLY, leaving QUESOBY, which 'Rebel' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsequy is a funeral rite, and a eulogy is the tribute spoken at such a ceremony.

clue.text: Cost accidentally picked up? That's not right!

indicators.note: not right means the letter R, for right, is taken away

parts.note: to hear something by chance is to have overheard it

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a price they happened to catch must be wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's not right!' reads as a complaint, but it removes R (right) from OVERHEARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A running business expense such as rent is a fixed outgoing.

clue.text: Mash representatives?

parts.note: read as M plus ash, and ash is the remains of a fire, also called embers
read as M plus ash, and ash is the remains of a fire, also called embers

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether delegates could be squashed like potatoes.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'Mash' as M + ash: the M stays, and ash becomes EMBERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Elected parliamentarians are called the members for their constituencies.

clue.text: May be tuna sandwiches always hot

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: tuna is one example of a fish
ever means always, as in for ever

explanation.surface: Tuna sandwiches are always served hot, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like food but is a verb: FISH holds EVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Running a high temperature from illness means being feverish.

clue.text: Decrepit Italian head of state, once a socialist

parts.note: the Doge was the elected ruler of Venice and Genoa
red is a common label for a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: A former Venetian ruler, once a leftist, has grown frail.
explanation.walkthrough: The Doge ruled the Venetian republic for centuries; RED for a left-winger is a standard crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Pages with folded corners look worn and shabby, hence old and battered.

clue.text: See 8
Denounced, rejected and free

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: reviled means attacked verbally, denounced

explanation.surface: A prisoner, condemned and turned away, is then released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' seems a second accusation, but it turns REVILED backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver someone from danger is to rescue or liberate them.

clue.text: Dismiss bears

definitions.meaning: two of the honey-loving bear of A. A. Milne's stories, named twice

explanation.surface: Someone sends some bears packing.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorn an idea is to brush it off, and Milne's teddy named twice makes a pair of bears.

clue.text: See 1 down
Romeo and Juliet possibly speculate about everyone

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to speculate is to gamble, to bet
all means everyone

explanation.surface: The fate of the star-crossed lovers is a gamble for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romeo and Juliet' is the Prokofiev work, not the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Prokofiev set the Shakespeare tragedy as a classical dance work, one example of the form.

clue.text: Martial art found in 50% of Taiwan and large part of China

indicators.note: fifty per cent of means the first half of the word Taiwan
large part of keeps most of the word China, dropping its last letters

explanation.surface: A fighting discipline is practised in half of Taiwan and much of China.
explanation.walkthrough: '50% of' takes the first three letters of 'Taiwan'; 'large part of' takes three of the five letters of 'China'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Chinese system of slow, flowing exercises began as a form of unarmed combat.

clue.text: Port bottles the ultimate in vintage — bliss!

indicators.note: bottles means contains, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a haven is a harbour or port

indicators.note: the ultimate in picks the final letter of the word vintage

explanation.surface: Port wine bottled from the best vintage is pure delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' and 'vintage' suggest wine, but the port is a harbour and 'bottles' means holds; E is the end of 'vintage'.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is a byword for perfect happiness.

clue.text: Friend a right nuisance in this city

parts.note: bud is American slang for a friend
a right nuisance is a real pest, right being a British intensifier

explanation.surface: A pal is a real pain in this capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' looks like R, but 'a right nuisance' is British for an utter nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hungarian capital is a city on the Danube.

clue.text: See 21
Kitty gulps medicine back and gets a sweet

indicators.note: back means the whole assembled piece is read in reverse
gulps means swallows, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a pool is a shared fund of money, a kitty
a pill is a dose of medicine

explanation.surface: A cat swallows its medicine and is rewarded with a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitty' is a fund, not a cat: POOL takes in PILL to give POPILLOL, which 'back' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard candy on a stick is a sweet, or a candy to Americans.

clue.text: Wings of saprophytic horse beetle

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its first and last letters, here of saprophytic

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: A beetle with wings feeds on decaying matter alongside a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wings' seems to belong to the beetle, but it takes the first and last letters of 'saprophytic', S and C.
explanation.definitionFit: The dung beetle was sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Wretched habit I developed for say, cheese

indicators.note: developed means worked out into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone confesses a bad habit they took up concerning cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' fits a photographer, like the answer, but rearranges WRETCHED HABIT I.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographers use both phrases to make subjects look at the camera and smile.
